Meet Sift

Your photos and videos, without the folder maze.

Sift opens a whole project folder, or a shared Google Drive, and shows every image and clip inside it in one clean grid. No downloads, no digging five folders deep, nothing uploaded anywhere.

Runs in your browser Nothing is uploaded Local folders or Google Drive
Open Sift →
What Sift is

A calm way to look through a mountain of media.

After a shoot or a product drop, the files pile up: hundreds of photos, a stack of short clips, buried in folders inside folders. Finding the right shot means clicking forever, and previewing a Drive folder properly is close to impossible.

Sift fixes that. Point it at a folder on your computer or a Google Drive folder, and every image and video across the whole nested structure loads into a single, scrollable grid. Think of the Adobe Bridge idea, except it is free, it runs in your browser, and it reads straight from Drive.

From there you can search, sort, rate, find your sharpest shots, and export exactly the ones you want, all in a few minutes.

Getting started

Two ways in. Both take under a minute.

Open kingadow.com/sift in Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge (these two browsers only). Then pick your source.

On your computer

Open a folder

  1. Click Open Folder, or drag a folder straight onto the window.
  2. Pick the project folder. Sift reads it in place, so nothing is copied or moved.
  3. Every photo and video appears in the grid, ready to browse.

Best for files already on your machine, or a Google Drive folder you sync with Drive for Desktop.

In the cloud

Connect Google Drive

  1. Click Google Drive and sign in with your Google account.
  2. Approve the read-only access, then choose a folder to browse.
  3. Your files, including anything shared with you, load into the grid.

Drive is invite-only for now. Sign in with the exact email address that was added to the guest list. If you see "access blocked," send that address over and it will be added.

Everything Sift does

Find it, look at it, pick the keepers, hand them off.

The whole tool is built around that one loop. Here is what lives in each step.

1

Find

get to the right shot in seconds

Smart search

Describe what you want in plain words, like "navy dress" or "food on a white plate," and the best matches rise to the top. No tagging needed.

Filters

Narrow by file type, star rating, colour, content category, or your own tags. Combine them to zero in on exactly the set you need.

Your own tags

Type any tag you like, such as Hero, Approved, Reshoot, or a campaign name, and Sift turns it into a filter and a group. Fully your system, however you organise.

Sort and group

Order by name, date, size, rating, or quality. Group the grid by folder, colour, category, your own tags, or near-duplicate cluster.

One grid, any depth

Turn on "include subfolders" and a whole nested project flattens into a single view, with a folder tree and live counts alongside.

2

See

preview without downloading a thing

Video, first class

Clips show a poster frame, a play badge, and their length. Hover to scrub, or open one to watch it in full.

Full-screen viewer

Open any shot large, move with the arrow keys, and zoom to 100% to check focus before you keep it.

Details panel

A resizable side panel shows a large preview plus the shot's date, camera, and location, with the image as big as you like.

Capture info

When available, Sift reads each shot's date taken and camera, and offers the location as a private map link only.

3

Choose

keep the best, skip the rest

Star ratings and notes

Rate as you go with a click or the number keys, add a note, then filter down to your five-star picks.

Find best shots

Sift scores each frame for sharpness and exposure, groups near-identical takes, and flags the single best shot in each pile.

Colour and auto tags

Match shots to a colour palette, or auto-label what is in them, then sort and group by either, all on your device.

Review your picks

Flip to a "view picks" mode to see only what you have selected, so you can sign off on the final set at a glance.

4

Hand off

deliver the exact set you chose

Download

One file goes straight to your Downloads folder. Several come as a single tidy zip, with no nested folders to dig through.

Spreadsheet export

Export your picks as a CSV with names, ratings, colours, tags, and notes, ready for whoever builds the page or edit.

Copy the file list

Copy the picked file names to your clipboard in one click, ready to paste into an email or a brief.

Come back to it

Reopening a folder is instant, and a reload keeps you right where you were instead of starting over.

For product photography

Optional: Claude writes the copy for your shots.

Opt-in

Turn picked images into ready-to-use words.

Select your product shots, and Claude writes alt text, a product description, and a social caption for each one, in your brand's voice. The results save with each image and drop straight into the CSV export.

Brand profiles

Set up a profile per brand with its voice, product names, and colour terms. Copy then reads "the Willow Romper in Dusty Pink," not "a pink garment."

How it stays private

This is the one optional cloud feature. Images are sent only when you press Generate, using your own key, and only for the shots you picked.

Your files stay yours

Private by design.

  • Nothing is uploaded. Your photos and videos stay where they live. Sift only reads and shows them.
  • Read-only, always. On your computer and in Drive, Sift can look but never change, move, or delete a file.
  • The clever parts run on your device. Search, tagging, and best-shot scoring all happen in your own browser.
  • One clear exception. The optional Claude copywriting sends only the images you pick, only when you press Generate.
Good to know

A few quick answers.

Which browser do I need?

Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge. These are the only two that support opening local folders and Google sign-in the way Sift needs. Safari and Firefox will not work.

Do I have to install anything?

No. Sift is a single web page. Open the link, and you are ready to go.

The first search is slow. Is that normal?

Yes. The first time you search a folder, Sift looks at every image once so it can understand them. That pass runs on your device and is saved, so every search after it is instant.

My Google Drive says "access blocked."

Drive is invite-only while the app is in testing. Sign in with the exact email that was added to the guest list. If yours has not been added yet, send it over and it takes a moment to add. The address must be a Google account.

A thumbnail did not load, or something looks off.

Hit the Refresh button in the toolbar, or reload the page. Sift heals stale previews on its own, and a reload keeps you in the same folder.
